issues.description: The Problem Statement and Template expect concrete classes named Goat, Pig, and Seal (students are asked to implement Goat, Seal, and Pig and Main/template reference these names), but the Solution repository does not provide implementations for Goat, Pig, or Seal (those files are empty) and instead provides implemented classes named SpaceGoat, SpacePig, and SpaceSeal. This class-name mismatch between the solution and the specification/template can confuse students who inspect the reference solution or try to run/compare it against the expected class names and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution repository with the problem/template by providing implementations for Goat, Pig, and Seal (matching the class names and behavior described in the problem) or, alternatively, update the problem statement and template to explicitly use the SpaceGoat/SpacePig/SpaceSeal class names. Ensure the reference solution includes the same class names and signatures students are instructed to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to animal classes named 'Seal', 'Pig', and 'Goat' (and expect their methods/messages to use those type names), but the solution implementation provides classes named 'SpaceSeal', 'SpacePig', and 'SpaceGoat'. This inconsistent naming breaks the straightforward mapping between the exercise requirements and the provided solution: students looking for Seal/Pig/Goat implementations in the solution will instead find differently named classes, and runtime messages (e.g. messageOnMilk/messageOnRide) will include the 'Space' prefix (e.g. 'SpaceSeal Clarabelle is milked') instead of the expected 'Seal Clarabelle is milked'. This creates unnecessary cognitive load and may cause confusion when students try to compare their work to the solution or understand expected outputs.
issues.suggestedFix: Align class names in the solution with the problem and template by renaming SpaceSeal -> Seal, SpacePig -> Pig, and SpaceGoat -> Goat (and update constructors and references accordingly). Also ensure messageOnMilk() and messageOnRide() produce messages using the expected animal type names (e.g., 'Seal <name> is milked', 'Riding on Pig <name>').
